messages.content: Ravi confirmed he can take April 3 to 7, so let's plan the full four nights. He wants to arrive before dinner the first day and come back after lunch on Monday if we can. Can you narrow this to a plan I can show him? I'm still torn between paying more for DCA and using BWI, and between the Penn Quarter roomier hotel and the Smithsonian one with breakfast.

Yes. One missing assumption before I call it final: baggage. I can compare with carry-ons only, but if you expect a checked bag either way, that changes the DCA versus BWI math. Provisional read: DCA is the smoother airport for a museum-heavy, no-car trip; BWI is still the budget lever. On hotels, the real tradeoff is four nights of room comfort and dinner access versus included breakfast.
Assume carry-ons and maybe one checked bag coming home if we buy souvenirs. No rental car.

With that, the flight lanes look like this: DCA option: nonstop ATL-DCA late morning Apr. 3, about 11:20 a.m. to 1:05 p.m.; return Apr. 7 around 1:45 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. About $1,215 for three before any checked bag. DCA rideshare to Penn Quarter is usually short, roughly 15 to 25 minutes. BWI option: nonstop ATL-BWI late morning and a 2-ish p.m. return, about $740 to $800 for three depending on fare bucket, with bags more favorable if the best fare is Southwest. After ground transfer, BWI still saves roughly $350 to $450, but it adds a 60 to 90 minute transfer each direction.
How bad is BWI with Leela and bags, practically?

Doable, not terrible, but it changes the feel of both travel days. With DCA, you can be at the hotel around 2:00 to 2:30, store bags if needed, and still have an easy first dinner. With BWI, the airport-to-hotel leg can push arrival closer to 3:30 or 4:00, especially if you wait for a train or rideshare. On Monday, BWI also means leaving the hotel earlier, so the after-lunch return becomes more of a quick bite than a relaxed lunch.
Okay. Now hotel choice. Ravi leaned toward room size, but he does like not having to figure out breakfast.

Hotel shortlist: Penn Quarter: about $326/night before taxes, 4.4-ish guest rating, larger family-friendly room, many casual dinner options within a short walk, easy Metro/rideshare access. Breakfast is paid. Smithsonian-area hotel: about $292/night, 4.3 guest rating, included breakfast, very convenient for morning museum starts, but the room is noticeably tighter for four nights. Capitol Hill: about $284/night, quiet and well-rated, but it is less convenient for the first two museum days and would add more Metro/rideshare friction. My pick for the full four nights is Penn Quarter unless keeping breakfast included is a stronger priority than space.
What's the rough all-in difference between the convenient version and the cheapest sensible version?

Roughly: DCA plus Penn Quarter is about $1,280 for flights/transfers before any checked bag plus $1,304 before hotel taxes, so call it around $2,580 before hotel taxes and meals. BWI plus Smithsonian is closer to $850 to $900 for flights/transfers plus $1,168 before hotel taxes, and breakfast is included, so around $2,050 before hotel taxes. The cheapest sensible version may save around $500 to $650, but it combines both tradeoffs: longer airport transfers and a tighter room.
Is there a middle option that doesn't sacrifice everything?

Two middle options: DCA plus Smithsonian keeps the easy airport and included breakfast, but you give up room space. That likely saves about $135 on room rate plus some breakfast spending. BWI plus Penn Quarter keeps the better room and restaurant access, while using the airport savings; that saves more, but the airport days are longer. I would not lead with Capitol Hill for this itinerary because the first two mornings are museum-focused.
What about a later DCA return? I saw something closer to dinner.

A later DCA return would give you more Monday time, but it is not my first choice before a school week. A 5:30 or 6:00 p.m. departure means getting home closer to 8:30 or 9:00 after baggage, MARTA or rideshare, and unpacking. The early-afternoon nonstop is the cleaner family option: checkout, early lunch or airport lunch, home before dinner.
And the late-morning outbound still gets us there before dinner?

Yes. Even allowing for DCA pickup and hotel check-in, you should have a low-pressure first afternoon. If the room is not ready, the Penn Quarter hotel can store bags, and you can do a snack or short walk before a 5:30-ish casual dinner.
Can you give me the Ravi version? Short bullets, with breakfast addressed.

Send him this: 1) Recommended plan: fly ATL-DCA nonstop Apr. 3 late morning, return Apr. 7 early afternoon, and stay in the larger Penn Quarter room. 2) Why: easiest airport transfers, better four-night room setup, and lots of nearby dinner choices. 3) Cost tradeoff: about $500 to $650 more than the most budget-conscious BWI plus Smithsonian version. 4) Breakfast tradeoff: Penn Quarter breakfast is paid, but there are quick cafes nearby; for museum mornings we can do grab-and-go instead of a sit-down hotel breakfast. 5) If he wants to save without shrinking the room, the fallback is BWI plus Penn Quarter.
That works. Leave it as Plan A pending one last price check. Don't book yet; I'll show Ravi tonight.

Plan A to hold for approval: Apr. 3 to 7, ATL-DCA nonstop late-morning outbound, early-afternoon return, Penn Quarter larger room, paid breakfast, no rental car. Watch points before booking: if the DCA fare jumps more than about $150 total, recompare BWI plus Penn Quarter; if the Penn Quarter room rises above about $340 before taxes or loses free cancellation, compare the Smithsonian breakfast option again.

No, it compresses the afternoon a bit but does not break the plan. You should still be at the Penn Quarter hotel midafternoon, store bags if the room is not ready, and have plenty of time for a casual dinner.

Then keep Thursday simple: arrive ATL about two hours before departure because it is spring-break season, and do carry-ons only. For Friday and Saturday, plan grab-and-go breakfast rather than a slow paid hotel breakfast before timed entries.
Can you check if better seats opened? Closer to the front is fine, but only if we stay together.

I would keep what you have. Outbound 18A/B/C and return 21A/B/C are still together, with you in the A window seat. The closer rows showing now split the three of you or trade into middle seats without much benefit.
Should I prebook a DCA car or just use rideshare when we land?

Use rideshare on arrival. DCA to Penn Quarter is short enough that prebooking adds more waiting risk than value. If you are not bringing a booster or car seat, just follow the DCA rideshare signs and expect roughly 15 to 25 minutes in the car.
No booster. Give me the final departure checklist.

Checklist: check in online the day before and recheck flight status and seats; add a checked bag only if packing changes. Leave Decatur around 8:15-8:30 for the late-morning ATL departure, earlier if you decide to check a bag. Pack IDs, museum timed-entry QR codes, light rain jackets, portable charger, and a small snack for Leela. At DCA, use rideshare to Penn Quarter; hotel can store bags if the room is not ready. Friday breakfast should be quick cafe or grab-and-go before the museum entry. Monday return: early lunch, check out, and leave the hotel around 11:45 for the 1:45 p.m. flight.
